pages.text: Independent observers began with local problems and invented different marks for what they found. Two records may disagree in notation yet describe the same typed relation.$(br2)A mathemagician compares their inputs, bindings, and result. Age, distance, and authority do not make a proof valid; a construction must survive inspection and use.

pages.title: Shared Records
pages.text: The Theorems catalog preserves modern reconstructions, not ownership. A field lineage means that a proof echoes one tradition's surviving method.$(br2)Hover a theorem to see that lineage. Future manuscripts may preserve alternate demonstrations, but a record never casts or rewrites a talisman by itself.
